topic: direction of travel per carriageway, 12F-Ams view

method.name: virtual tripwire / motion-energy cross-correlation
method.detail: Decode 4 fps to 480x270 greyscale. Motion energy = mean |frame(k+1) - frame(k)| inside a band. Two bands per carriageway, one upstream of the other; cross-correlate their time series over lags of +/-24 frames (+/-6 s). The band that leads is the one traffic arrives at first, so the lag sign gives the direction.
method.why_not_optical_flow: Phase correlation on 96 px windows failed twice: at 2 fps a vehicle moves ~100 px at 960 px width, far beyond the search range, and once the range was widened the window is >95% static asphalt so the correlation peak locks onto zero shift. Tripwires are immune to static background.

judgement: Band rectangles placed by eye from a single frame. Motion threshold 2.0, minimum 25 samples, and the +/-24 frame search range were all chosen, not derived. The call that r=0.50 and r=0.82 are believable while r=0.16 and r=0.35 are noise is a judgement; the 4 s lag on the cross street was rejected on physical grounds (too long for the distance), which is also a judgement. Right-hand driving was invoked as external corroboration for the avenue result — that is an assumption about the jurisdiction, not a measurement.

avenue.layout: two-way, split by a double yellow line (read directly off the pavement, not inferred)
avenue.corroboration: The two sides disagree in sign, which is what a two-way street with right-hand driving must produce. Two independent measurements agreeing with an external constraint.

cross_street.why: Both correlations are noise. The cross street is the side under construction: cones, barriers and workers moving on the spot contribute motion energy that swamps the traffic signal. The south-half lag of 4 s is also physically impossible over that distance.
cross_street.eyeball_observation: Two distinctive vehicles traced by hand — a USPS tractor-trailer at 110-120 s and an MTA bus at 103-107 s — both travelled RIGHT to LEFT. That is an observation of two vehicles, not a measurement of the carriageway, and it does not exclude a lane running the other way.

reliability.supports: Saying which side of the avenue's double yellow carries which direction. Enough to adjudicate a wrong-way claim about a road user whose side of the line is known.
reliability.does_not_support: Any claim about the cross street. Any compass label — the measurement is in image space (up/down/left/right); mapping those to N/S/E/W needs the street layout, which has not been established from this view.
reliability.known_gap: A wrong-way judgement needs BOTH the direction of travel AND which side of the double yellow the road user is on. The 2026-08-29 probe run reported two wrong-way cyclists as travelling 'towards top right' without stating the side, so those claims are unadjudicable as written.
